rules: Caption polarity is a class property here: every figure caption is printed under its art, every table caption above the first rule, and the two page-furniture graphics (the foot follow-card and the memo banner) carry no caption at all [caption.position].

The paper numbers its tables with Roman numerals - TABLE II to TABLE VII - which the numbering vocabulary cannot express, so numbering reads 'none' on all six tables while the printed form survives untouched in the caption verbatim string [caption.numbering].

Every figure caption is a bare noun phrase: no unit, no condition, no claim and no verb, so units, conditions and concludes are false and voice is none across all nineteen figure rows [caption.verbatim].
The pink QR card reprinted at the page foot is furniture, not an exhibit: the same 693-path strip recurs on nine pages in the bottom band and is refused each time [place.page_zone].

A notation-table row that straddles the page break is extracted as a wide, very flat colour block and looks like a display equation until the crop is opened; the symbol and its definition between two rules make it a fragment of the 2.2 Notations table [place.area_frac].

Multi-plate figures are one row per measured plate and never one merged row, whether the plates sit side by side on one page (Fig.6 three up, Fig.8 two up) or split across a page break (Fig.11 and Fig.12 two each, Fig.13 two plus one); merging them leaves a measured region unaccounted [geometry.panel_count].

The three Fig.6 plates are numbered out of reading order in the PDF object stream - region 1 is the middle plate, region 2 the right, region 3 the left - and because their top edges differ by under two points the measured y-then-x sort also reads them centre, right, left. doc_order is left exactly as measured and the misordering is stated in the notes rather than corrected [place.doc_order].

The two map pairs share one frame but not one key: the risk pair uses a stepped four-swatch bar with named classes and no printed number, the GCI pair a continuous ramp with ticks 0.0-1.0, so printed_numbers is true for the GCI plates and false for the risk plates [geometry.printed_numbers].

A colour key can be a colour bar without printing any number: the stepped Risk Levels bar is a real colorbar with four labelled swatches and zero ticks, which is why colorbar is true on it while printed_numbers is false [geometry.colorbar].

Bar charts in this paper print their values as labels on the marks and often have no numbered axis at all - Fig.1 has neither rule nor tick, only the counts at the bar ends - so data_labels and printed_numbers have to be read separately and can disagree [geometry.data_labels].
Fig.9 carries a broken x axis (0-25, diagonal slashes, 300-600+) and is still a bar chart; the axis break is an annotation and not a second panel or a change of family [geometry.family].

Panels of one figure do not share a scale by default: the three Fig.13 bars print on 0-200, 0-100 and 0-120 with two bars clipped past the top tick in each, and the Fig.8 pair differs 27-fold in y (0-800 then 0-30), so shared_axes is false for both figures even where the x ticks are identical [geometry.shared_axes].

Fig.13 conveys its three policy classes by bar colour alone - blue, orange, green - with no legend in any of the three panels, so legend is none on all three rows and the class names survive only as the A_I / B_II category tick labels [geometry.legend].

The six tables use two constructions and nothing else: TABLE II and III are rule-light with three horizontal rules and no side edges, TABLES IV to VII are fully boxed two-or-three-row matrices with an empty top-left stub cell [table.rule_style].

No table in this paper puts a unit in a header or in a cell: the six tables carry years, counts, index scores and correlation coefficients with bare numbers, so units_in_header is false throughout [table.units_in_header].

Decimal alignment follows the numeric columns and not the table: it holds in TABLE III-VII, whose value columns share a decimal point, and fails in TABLE II, which is two text columns of URLs [table.decimal_aligned].

Numbers in the prose run below the printed captions in section 4.1 - the sentence 'illustrated in Figure 9 below' points at printed Fig.11 and 'Figure 10 below illustrates the GCI' at printed Fig.12, while the 4.1 recap of section 2.3 says 'Figure 4 and Figure 5' for printed Fig.3 and Fig.4. The pointer spelling is recorded as printed and the defect is not repaired [mention.style].
One pointer lost its digit in typesetting: Fig.9 is named once in the whole paper and only as 'As shown in Figure M', so its style field carries that spelling verbatim [mention.style].

Panels printed on p20 are first named on p21, after the art, so their lead_pages is negative - the honest value of exhibit page minus first mention page, not an error to be fixed by pushing first_page forward [mention.lead_pages].

Two exhibits are never named in prose at all: Fig.3 is skipped outright and Fig.6 is referred to only as 'From the chart above', so first_page is null and the printed caption is the only naming either of them gets [mention.first_page].

Two exhibits are pointed at only by a deictic 'the figure and table below' with no number at all, so Fig.14 and TABLE VII carry an empty style list and lead_pattern none while still being correctly placed on their own page [mention.lead_pattern].

A figure's plates and its caption can fall on different pages: the Fig.11 caption sits on p19 under plate (b) while plate (a) is on p18, and both rows are recorded with that one caption, so caption polarity alone cannot place a row [caption.position].

The four (a)-(d) callout boxes inside Fig.10 are insets of one model schematic, not separate plates, so panel_count stays 1 and the composition is described in the note instead of being counted [geometry.panel_count].

The printed caption numbers jump from Fig.4 to Fig.6 to Fig.8 only because pages 9, 10 and 12 were inserted into this PDF as rasters: their prose is visible in the render but absent from the text layer, and the region pass measures nothing on them. Fig.5 is printed on p9 and Fig.7 on p12, so two real figures carry no measured region and stay unrecorded; the gap is recorded here and not filled by guessing a bbox [caption.numbering].
